pageTitle: Apply to suspend (stop or delay) the eviction
caption: Make an application
heading: Apply to suspend (stop or delay) the eviction
paragraph1: You can ask a judge to ‘suspend the warrant for possession’. This means delaying the eviction or allowing you to stay in your home if you are able to make payments again.
paragraph2: A new hearing will be held but the judge will not automatically agree to suspend the possession warrant - it depends what happens in court.
ifCourtApprovesHeading: If the court approves your request to suspend the eviction
ifCourtApprovesParagraph1: If the court approves your request: you may be able to stay in your home, either temporarily or indefinitely, if you meet certain conditions. For example the judge could ask you to set up a payment plan so that you can repay the rent or mortgage payments you owe.
ifCourtApprovesParagraph2: If you do not meet the conditions, you can be evicted.
ifCourtRefusesHeading: If the court refuses your request to suspend the eviction
ifCourtRefusesParagraph: If the court refuses your request, you will need to leave the property.
ifYouCanPayTheCourtFee: if you can pay the court fee, or if you need help with fees (help to pay court fees)
whyYouAreAskingTheCourt: why you are asking the court to suspend the warrant
youWillAlsoNeedEvidence: You’ll also need to provide some evidence for the judge.
reviewTime: It usually takes up to 10 working days for the court to review your application and make a decision once you have paid.
suspendCost: It costs {{suspendFee, currency(currency: GBP; trailingZeroDisplay: stripIfInteger)}} to apply to suspend the eviction.
moreThanOneThing: If you ask the court for more than one thing, you may need to pay more.
ifYouAreWorriedAboutPayingFees: If you are worried about paying fees
helpWithFees: You may be eligible to apply for help with fees (GOV.UK, opens in a new tab). We recommend you apply for help with fees before you apply to suspend, because we will ask you to provide a help with fees reference number when you apply.
ifPreferToRespondByPost: If you’d prefer to respond by post:
fillInFormForPost: fill in the N244 form
sendTheCompletedFormToTheCourt: send the completed form to the court
